data.content_ref: inline:Add support edges as defender edges: for each support relation B supports A and each attacker C of A, add an edge B→C. This lets an accepted supporter B defeat A's attackers, strengthening A within the same grounded fixpoint. The graph remains an AF, so determinism, polynomial cost, and derived reinstatement are preserved; committed roots are untouched by the added edges. Weakness: support becomes a universal counterattack and cannot express degrees of support; a single accepted supporter can overturn many independent attacks, and the semantics depends on choosing which supports are active before the fixpoint.
